newsitem.title: SPAIN: Members of death squads still around, Spain says.
newsitem.headline: Members of death squads still around, Spain says.

text.p: Some members of the so-called "dirty warriors" death squads who killed 28 people in an illegal campaign against Basque separatists in the 1980s may still be at large and active, Spain's interior minister said on Wednesday.
"There are perhaps residues, perhaps some groups that are still acting," Jaime Mayor Oreja said in a radio interview.
It was the first admission by the new conservative government that members of the security forces and hired gunmen who fought the illegal campaign are still at large.
Mayor Oreja was commenting on the kidnapping and torture last week of a key witness in "dirty war" trials.

The previous Socialist administration's first interior minister and top civilian and military officials are on trial for setting up and funding the death squads that operated under the acronym of GAL (Anti-Terrorist Liberation Groups).

A protected witness who has implicated top Civil Guard general Enrique Rodriguez Galindo in the first two killings in 1983 was abducted last Friday, tortured with cigarettes and sodomised by attackers who told him to alter his testimony.

Mayor Oreja gave no further details, said it was too early to know whether members of the paramilitary Civil Guard were involved. He insisted in the interview that the only real terrorist group at work in Spain was ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
